description:
Add a long-term memory record to a character (PC or NPC). The memory lives in the sheet itself, survives history compaction (chapters), and is always visible to the planner and the implementors in subsequent turns.

        |The types (`type`) are mutually exclusive, choose exactly one by content:
        |- `EVENT` — a one-time plot event that happened and left a mark (the death of a loved one, an escape from captivity, found an artifact, survived a catastrophe). This is "a fact of what happened". Not for relationships (RELATIONSHIP) and not for information (KNOWLEDGE).
        |- `RELATIONSHIP` — a lasting relationship with a **specific** other character (ally/enemy/mentor/lover/debtor/blood enemy/rival). Exists over time. A shift in the relationship per the plot is a new understanding: close the previous record and write a new one under a new `memoryTextId`. Do not confuse with IMPRESSION (a one-off assessment).
        |- `OBLIGATION` — an **INTERNAL** oath, vow, a personal promise to oneself or loved ones. The source is **inside** the character. No outside employer, no reward from outside. **Do not confuse with QUEST**: if there is someone who hired/commissioned/asked from outside — it is a QUEST, not an OBLIGATION.
        |- `KNOWLEDGE` — learned information (a secret, a fact, a rumor, a name, a location, a secret). "What the character now knows". Do not confuse with EVENT (there it is an event; here it is information).
        |- `REPUTATION` — a **group** opinion of the character in a faction/location/guild/layer of society. Do not confuse with IMPRESSION (the opinion of one NPC).
        |- `IMPRESSION` — **FOR NPCs ONLY**. The subjective impression of **one** NPC about someone/something: a PC, **another NPC**, a place, a faction, an event. NPC↔NPC impressions are just as important: they make the world alive (NPCs react to each other in scenes — ally, dislike, despise). Not allowed for a PC — an error will be returned. `directive` is especially important — it literally dictates the NPC's behavior.
        |- `QUEST` — an **EXTERNAL** contract, hire, commission from a client (an NPC, a guild, a faction, a note). Usually there is a goal and a reward. The UI separately shows the active QUEST as a counter on the character's portrait. **Any paid work of a PC = QUEST.**

        |Edge cases:
        |- A PC swore to avenge their parents themself → OBLIGATION. A PC hired by a merchant to find the killers for money → QUEST.
        |- A PC's first meeting with an NPC → IMPRESSION (for the NPC). When the relationship has already been established over time → RELATIONSHIP as a separate record under a new `memoryTextId`, close the previous IMPRESSION as `OUTDATED`.
        |- A MILESTONE / progress on a quest (a stage on the way to the goal: reached the place, defeated the guardian, found the key) is NOT closing the quest. Record the milestone with a SEPARATE EVENT with a `RELATES_TO` link to the QUEST record; do NOT touch the quest's own status. A QUEST is moved to COMPLETED (via updateMemory) ONLY when its goal's wording itself has been achieved, not an intermediate victory.

        |Gesture and id. `addMemory` — "the character remembered something new": new knowledge and new understanding are written only under a NEW `memoryTextId`. If the understanding changed per the plot (a rumor turned out false, an impression changed, a deal was terminated) — close the previous record (`updateMemory` with `status=OUTDATED` and `outcome`, or via the new one's `closes` parameter) and write a new one. An existing id (including that of a lifted record) is rejected: refining the same record and returning a lifted one — via `updateMemory`.

        |Fields:
        |- `fact` — what happened objectively, without emotions. At least 20 characters.
        |- `context` — the personal meaning for **this** character: emotions, assessment, with whom they are ready to share, secrecy. In their voice in the first person. If the context is personal — explicitly mark "does not share with the first person they meet" or "only with X", otherwise the narrative agent may blurt it out.
        |- `directive` (optional) — **FOR NPCs ONLY**. A behavioral stance for the NPC in future turns. For a PC — null (controlled by a live player).
        |- `importance` — LOW/NORMAL/HIGH, for resolving contradictions between directives.
name: addMemory

description:
Add a new character state (Blinded, Poisoned, Bear Transformation, Concentration on a spell, etc.).
        |⏳ The state's timer is in SECONDS of game time (durationSeconds): round = 6, minute = 60, hour = 3600. The server immediately stamps the moment of staleness (expiresAtClock) IN THE CARRIER'S TIME — "for an hour" means an hour of THEIR time, and spells tick in battle and out of it alike.
        |⛔ A STATE MUST HAVE AN END. When setting a state, you must answer HOW IT WILL END, and record the answer in exactly one of two ways (both is allowed):
        |  • a DEADLINE — `durationSeconds` (invisibility for 1 hour → 3600, a blessing for 10 rounds → 60). The server stamps the moment of staleness, and then the state is removed by the clock;
        |  • a TRIGGER — the end condition IN WORDS in `duration`: "fades when the character attacks or casts", "until concentration ends", "until a long rest", "while holding the torch". The trigger must be verifiable by the playing out, not "while in effect".
        |A spell/potion/ability effect WITHOUT both is a defect: such a state will hang on the character forever, and no scene master will remove it. An empty deadline AND trigger are legal ONLY for a substantively PERMANENT state (a curse until removed by a ritual, an innate trait, a maiming, a cult mark) — and then write exactly that in `duration` ("permanent, until removed by a ritual").
        |⛔ The SECRET `secret` is REQUIRED at the birth of a state, there is no default: "all" — public, visible to the player; "nobody" — hidden, nobody knows except the carrier; a list of UUIDs — exactly they know.
        |If a state with that stateId already exists — an error: change it with `updateState`, remove with `removeState`, and only then set anew. When it ended — remove with `removeState` and play out the ending in the narrative.
name: addState

name.description: Short state name (what the player sees in the UI).

description.description: Description of effects (≤ 200 characters): what the state does to the character.

value.description: Structured value, if any: '-10' for a Strength debuff, '3 charges', 'to 0 HP', 'brown bear'. null — a state without a numeric/short value.

duration.description: HOW THE STATE ENDS, in words for the player and for the scene master: a duration ('1 round', '1 hour') and/or a VERIFIABLE TRIGGER CONDITION ('fades when it attacks or casts', 'until concentration ends', 'until a long rest'). If durationSeconds is not set — a trigger here is REQUIRED, except for states that are permanent in substance (and then write 'permanent, until removed by a ritual'). null — only for a permanent one.

durationSeconds.description: How long the effect LASTS, in seconds of the CARRIER's time (round=6, minute=60, hour=3600, 8 hours=28800). null — ONLY if the end of the state is described by a trigger in duration or the state is permanent.

source.description: textId of the state source (spell/attack/ability; 'master' — if it is a master's decision). null — not specified.

anyOf.description: all — public state, nobody — nobody knows except the carrier.

description:
Update an existing memory. Use for:
        |- Refining the fact/context/directive of the same record (details were added, the wording was corrected). If the understanding changed per the plot — not here: close the record (`OUTDATED`) and write a new one via `addMemory` under a new `memoryTextId`.
        |- **Fixing a wrongly chosen type (`type`).** Changing `type` is only a fix of a selection mistake: the record described from the very beginning the same thing as now, and the type was chosen wrongly. If the record became different because something happened after it (a rumor was confirmed, a meeting grew into a relationship, a secret gave rise to a vow, an act changed the attitude of those around), — that is a new understanding: close the old one (`OUTDATED`) and write a new one of the right type via `addMemory` under a new id. The test — compare with the moment of writing: a type that was correct **at the moment of writing** differs from the recorded one — this is a selection mistake, fix it with `updateMemory`. The type was correct at the moment of writing but became wrong because of **subsequent** events — this is a new memory via `addMemory`. The restrictions are the same as for addMemory: IMPRESSION only for NPCs; directive not for a PC.
        |- **Status changes (`status` + `outcome`)** in this turn: ACTIVE — active (this is how a lifted one is returned), COMPLETED — successfully, FAILED — failed, ABANDONED — withdrawn/refused, OUTDATED — the rumor/fact turned out false or lost relevance (this is how the previous understanding is closed before a new record).

        |⚠️ A MILESTONE ≠ CLOSURE. `status=COMPLETED` is set ONLY when the quest goal's wording ITSELF (fact) has been achieved: the quest "stop the ritual" is closed by the ritual being STOPPED, not by "reached the altar" / "the guardian is defeated" / "we stand at the threshold". Intermediate progress (a milestone, a stage, a local victory on the way to the goal) is NOT finalization: record it with a SEPARATE memory (a new EVENT with a RELATES_TO link to the quest), WITHOUT changing status. If you moved an active quest to COMPLETED on a milestone — the campaign's goal was silently closed with a fake outcome.

        |Pass only the fields that change. If you set a final status — be sure to give an outcome with a short description of the result ("The maps were handed to Crow, the reward received", "Crow refused to pay the remainder").
name: updateMemory

description:
Clone an already created/existing NPC as the basis for a new one — for a SERIES of identical ones (extras of one role: guards, bandits, rank-and-file goblins). A server-side copy: the inherent part (race, classes, stats, attacks, spells, features, proficiencies, inventory, look) is taken from the source; the VOLATILE is reset (HP = maximum, states and charges clean, memory empty). The LOOK (portrait/token) — BY REFERENCE to the source's look: a second image generation is NOT launched (several guards — one token).

SERIES PATTERN (when a task asks for N identical enemies/NPCs): mold the FIRST fully with an ordinary createCharacter + setters (with a textId like `guard-1`), the REST — cloneCharacter from the first (`guard-1` → `guard-2`, `guard-3`), then optionally pinpoint customization with ordinary update tools (name, 1-2 distinctions). This is cheaper than molding each from scratch: 1 full sheet + (N-1) clones instead of N full ones.

ERROR if the source does not exist, if newTextId is already taken, or if the source is a PLAYER or LEAD (we do not clone them: a PC is always bespoke, LEAD faces are unique).
name: cloneCharacter

newTextId.description: textId of the new clone — a unique slug (for example, `watchman-campfire-2`).

description:
Create a new character/NPC. Set the name, race, alignment, appearance, backstory and significance level. ERROR if a character with that textId already exists — use updateBasicInfo/updateNarrativeInfo to update.

AUTO-EFFECT: createCharacter automatically puts a request to generate the `base` appearance (uses `appearanceDescription` as the image prompt and `significance` as the render level). A separate `generateAppearance` after creation does NOT need to be called — an extra tool call.

When a NON-STANDARD starting look is needed (an NPC immediately in wild-shape / polymorph, after being wounded, in special armor) — after createCharacter call `generateAppearance(textId, "<custom-slug>", "<description>")`. This will overwrite the auto-base request in the queue — the image phase will generate exactly one appearance (the last by textId that you passed).
name: createCharacter

appearanceDescription.description: Detailed appearance description (used both as the image prompt for auto-generating the base appearance and for future choose-by-description). SELF-SUFFICIENT — STRICTLY about this ONE character: without mentioning other characters (by name or role), their actions and mutual poses (no "reaching for the Knight", "over the corpse of …", "next to …", "standing before …"). Otherwise the image model will draw two — this is a defect (its rules forbid several characters).

significance.description: Significance level. BACKGROUND — an extra (token only); MINOR — a secondary NPC (token only); MAJOR — a significant NPC (token+portrait); LEAD — a key plot NPC or companion (token+portrait+deep development). Determines what the auto-base appearance will draw.

description: Request generation of a character appearance variant (portrait/token — by significance). Cost: a portrait+token pair (MAJOR/LEAD) ~\$0.07; a single token (BACKGROUND/MINOR) ~\$0.034. description: Record a finding in the REVIEW phase: a concrete VIOLATION OF THE SHEET-BUILDING RULES — "the attack bonus does not match the modifier + proficiency bonus", "more spells than the class limit", "current hp above the maximum", "props from the order did not land in the inventory", "the profile does not match the significance". Record a violation REGARDLESS of whether your work introduced it or it came from the prototype. A matter of taste (you would have chosen another spell) is NOT a finding. No violations — do NOT call addFinding AT ALL: an empty review = finish; a ritual "everything is fine" finding is FORBIDDEN (it only burns an extra fix cycle). Do NOT call transitionTo — the frame will transition itself.
name: addFinding

description.description: Specific description: what exactly in the sheet does not add up and for whom.

severity.description: Criticality. CRITICAL — must be fixed; HIGH — serious; NORMAL — an improvement.

description: Write a note to the REQUESTER about what you did: they see the sheet but not your decisions, and it is exactly those that they need to play out/plan further. A PLAYER'S ORDER (the wizard): exactly one INFO is MANDATORY — what was assembled/changed briefly by items and what justifies it where you chose for them; they will see it next to their sheet, you must not stay silent. AN ORDER FROM THE GAME (the scene master, the stager, the combat planner): INFO is NOT mandatory — the sheet may have no player addressee at all, and a ritual note "into nowhere" burns a round-trip; write it only if the requester has something to learn beyond the sheet itself. Who your requester is is stated in the phase description. A repeat INFO REPLACES the previous one (in the end at most one INFO). WARNING and QUESTION ACCUMULATE and are appropriate for ANY requester: WARNING — the order was fulfilled DIFFERENTLY or not in full (including a forced substitution by class limit: removed a spell/feature for the sake of a new one); QUESTION — something was lacking, and only the requester can answer (they alone see the book, the scene and the request). Write in living language, not a technical log.
name: addPlayerNote

type.description: Type. INFO — the mandatory final note "what was done and why" (a repeat replaces it). WARNING — done differently/not in full. QUESTION — an answer from the requester is needed.

text.description: Note text in the game language. Brief and to the point.

description: Escalate the WHOLE order — ONLY when it cannot be expressed with your tools: the order requires changing the class/race/subclass/base concept of an ALREADY ASSEMBLED sheet (the class and race setters are yours for ASSEMBLING a sheet; changing the foundation of a finished one is rebuilding the character, not an edit) or redrawing the look when there is no look tool in your list. The yardstick is INSTRUMENTAL — by YOUR actual tool list, NOT "hard/large-scale". That list DIFFERS between orders (what there is nobody to execute — looks without a generator, states/memory/scene outside an ongoing game — is not mounted for you at all), so read the yardstick literally: no tool in the list — this work is not yours. And vice versa: picking spells and features, a combat profile, a level, props, depth of development by significance, recomputing derived values — are expressible with setters, this is YOUR work, do not escalate them. A refusal on ONE address is not an escalation but rejectOrder: escalation throws out the work on the WHOLE order. The call ENDS the work immediately — it is the last tool. In REVIEW the tool is also available and rightful there, when the review uncovered a heap of violations that your work did not introduce (the sheet is systemically broken).
name: escalate

reason.description: Specific reason: what exactly the tools lacked (not vague).

description: Search the library for a READY-MADE character for a role from the order — BEFORE molding from scratch. The query is a role description in words (race/archetype/occupation/demeanor), not a name. Returns a list of candidates with display HANDLES (`lib:…`) and descriptors. If one fits — instantiatePrototype with that handle: you get a READY sheet (race, classes, stats, attacks, spells, features) and the LOOK WITHOUT A SECOND GENERATION — then you only adapt it to the order. If none fit — say so when closing (in a note or in the review: which handle you looked at and why it does not fit), and mold from scratch.
name: findPrototypes

query.description: Role description for search: race/archetype/occupation ("an old city-gate guard", "an overgrown swamp toad").

description: Take a ready-made character from the library for an ORDER ADDRESS: the service copies the prototype's full sheet (race, classes, stats, attacks, spells, features, proficiencies, inventory), resets the volatile (HP=maximum, states/charges/memory clean) and attaches the LOOK BY REFERENCE — there will be no second image generation. After this the sheet ALREADY exists: do not create it anew (createCharacter will return an ERROR) and do not rewrite it entirely — ADAPT it to the order (name, role, 1-2 distinctions, props). ⏳ You will see the sheet's contents in the snapshot in the NEXT response — do not invent what ended up in it. The reference is exactly the display HANDLE (`lib:…`) from findPrototypes or a bare book NPC key from the book registry; a raw UUID is not accepted.
name: instantiatePrototype

ref.description: Reference to a prototype: a display handle (`lib:…`) from findPrototypes or a book NPC key from the book registry.

textId.description: The address under which we put the sheet — EXACTLY from the order (do not invent your own slug: the server owns the addresses).

newName.description: Instance name. null — the prototype's name is used (you can rename later with updateBasicInfo).

description: DECLINE ONE order address with a reason — when exactly this character cannot be assembled (the order contradicts the scene's canon, demands what is not in the rules, or the edit's addressee is not the one they were passed off as). A refusal is a legitimate answer: the requester will see the reason and decide themselves — play on without this face or approach differently. It does NOT cancel the other addresses of the order: you keep assembling them. Silently skipping an address is not allowed — it is lost work with no trace.
name: rejectOrder

textId.description: Address from the order that you are declining.

reason.description: Specific reason for the requester: why it cannot be assembled (not vague).

description: Move to the next phase of work. Call LAST in the response, when the current phase's work is done: the transition is applied at the END of this response, all the other calls of this same response still execute in the current phase. If some tool of this response returned "ERROR:", the transition is delayed and the turn returns to you in the current phase — first fix the failure.
name: transitionTo
